Subject: ACME Health — model fit & streaming quality follow-ups

Hi Sam / Asha — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same page:

Summary of discovery:
- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant for patient intake (short clinical notes -> structured summary + suggested triage level).
- Volume: ~5k requests/day initially, spiky up to 15k/day during peak hours.
- Quality priorities: high precision on triage suggestions, avoid hallucinations (safety), and fast partial streaming for better UX in the web client.
- Compliance: SOC 2 and data residency controls required for production.

Immediate asks from your side:
1) Recommendations for model variants to try for a proof-of-concept.
2) Sample prompt set + test harness to run a quality regression.
3) Streaming behavior tuning to avoid partial output incoherence and to control stop sequences.

Our recommended next steps:
- Action: We’ll deliver a curated prompt set and a benchmark PDF with per-model tradeoffs (attached). (Marissa/Jordan) — by EOD 2026-06-01.
- Action: Schedule a 60-min eval session with our SRE/solutions engineer to run live streaming tests (we suggest Wed 6/3). (Sam/Asha) — confirm availability.
- Action: HubSpot/POC mutual action plan and milestone doc — I’ve created a stub link below. (Marissa)

High-level model recommendations for POC:
- rw-13b-q4f16 (quantized) — good balance of cost and coherent streaming; recommended default for initial POC.
- rw-7b-ggml — fast and inexpensive for lower-sensitivity triage flows and heavy parallelism.
- rw-70b (fp16) — for the highest quality checks (sanity sampling and safety-critical fallback) — can be used as an async verifier.

Notes on streaming UX (summary):
- Partial output coherence: often caused by aggressive chunking combined with short stop sequences. We recommend incremental flush every 80–120 tokens with a 200ms max buffer and a heuristic to backfill previous chunk if we detect a sentence boundary mismatch.
- Stop sequences: prefer explicit stop tokens in prompts (e.g., "

### END") and post-process to trim trailing fragments.
- Latency: for your expected volume, start with small batching (batch window 10–25ms) and tune upwards; we can pin dedicated capacity if throughput SLOs are required.

Attachments included: acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts + expected outputs), redwood-benchmark-acme-20260601.pdf (per-model latency/cost/quality).

Let me know if you want us to include a quick SOC 2 checklist for the POC environment in the same packet. I’ll loop Jordan on the eval session details once we have a time.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our engineering team after looking at the attachments: 

1) Partial output coherence: our UX team is seeing cases where the streaming response returns a fragment (e.g., "recommend immediate...") and then the next chunk restarts a sentence leading to confusing UI. Is the backfill approach you mentioned automatic in the runtime or something we handle client-side?

2) Stop sequences: we use a combination of tokens and pattern matching. If we add an explicit "### END" stop, will that interfere with the quality/regression metrics?

3) Latency: our SLA target for interactive flows is <= 300ms tail p95. Is that realistic for rw-13b-q4f16 with your hosted offering, or do we need Dedicated?

Also related: we need to keep an audit trail of model versions and prompt sets used for regulatory review. Can your platform pin a model+prompt snapshot for an audit window?

Happy to run the eval session — Wed 6/3 after 1pm PT would work for our team.

—Sam

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>

@Sam — great questions, answers below + proposed next steps. Quoting your points for clarity.

On Tue, Jun 2, 2026 at 9:02 AM Sam Patel <sam@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> 1) Partial output coherence: our UX team is seeing cases where the streaming response returns a fragment (e.g., "recommend immediate...") and then the next chunk restarts a sentence leading to confusing UI. Is the backfill approach you mentioned automatic in the runtime or something we handle client-side?

Short answer: runtime + client coordination. Long answer: Redwood’s streaming runtime supports an optional chunk-backfill mode that detects sentence boundaries and re-sends the last ~40–80 tokens of the previous chunk when the next chunk begins mid-sentence. That is enabled server-side and results in smoother UX with only a small increase in tokens. For minimal token overhead you can also implement a client-side heuristic that hides a partial last line until the next chunk arrives; we can demo both in the eval session.

> 2) Stop sequences: we use a combination of tokens and pattern matching. If we add an explicit "### END" stop, will that interfere with the quality/regression metrics?

It won’t break the metrics — in fact explicit stop tokens are the cleanest way to guarantee truncated outputs and make regression comparison deterministic. We recommend: include the explicit stop token in the golden outputs for evaluations and strip it during presentation to users. The benchmark PDF includes a short section on deterministic evaluation with stop tokens.

> 3) Latency: our SLA target for interactive flows is <= 300ms tail p95. Is that realistic for rw-13b-q4f16 with your hosted offering, or do we need Dedicated?

For rw-13b-q4f16 on hosted: 300ms p95 is attainable for shorter sequences (<=128 tokens) with our low-latency routing and small batching policy. For your spike profile and stricter p95 we typically recommend:
- Start on hosted with reserved throughput (we can set a soft capacity for the POC).
- If you require guaranteed 300ms p95 under full peak, Dedicated capacity is the most predictable route (we provide SLA-backed latency targets in Dedicated).

> Audit trail: can your platform pin a model+prompt snapshot for an audit window?

Yes — Redwood supports immutable evaluation snapshots: you can pin a model version + prompt set + config and we’ll persist the mapping with a snapshot id (immutable). That snapshot id can be exported in our audit logs. We’ll add a snapshot for the POC prompts and record it to the HubSpot deal record.

Attachments/links for eval session: I uploaded the live eval harness and a short checklist to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cACME-eval. Also attaching the prompt set again here.
